 Order

Accused No.1 is before this court with a prayer to set aside the order dated 20.03.2024 passed by the Court of Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru in Spl.C.C.No.643/2023 rejecting the application filed by the petitioner under section 311 of Cr.P.C, with a prayer to recall the victim-PW1 for further cross examination.

sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent no.1.
3.

The petitioner is facing prosecution for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366(A), 376 of IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of POCSO Act before the trial NC: 2024:KHC:15197 court in Spl.C.No.643/2023.
In the said case, the victim has been examined as PW1 before the trial court on 31.07.2023 and she was cross-examined by defence on 17.08.2023.
Thereafter, the prosecution has examined the other witnesses and the investigating officer has been examined by the prosecution as PW9.
He was also cross- examined.
On the application of accused No.1, PW9 was recalled and he was further cross-examined on 19.02.2024.
Thereafter, application had filed under Section 311 of Cr.P.C, to recall PW1 for further cross- examination and the same was rejected by the trial court.
Therefore, the petitioner is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there are certain contradictions which was pointed to PW9 during his further cross-examination.
Therefore, it is necessary to further cross-examine PW1, who is the victim in the present case.
The trial court has dismissed the application.
As a result, fair trial is denied to the petitioner.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
Per contra, learned HCGP has seriously opposed the prayer made in the petition.
He submits that this is the third application made by accused no.1 for recalling PW1.
PW1 has been extensively Sri.

sentences.text: The victim is a minor and therefore she cannot be repeatedly recalled to adduce evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.

6. The material on record would go to show that the petitioner had earlier filed similar application under section 311 of Cr.P.C, before the trial court and the same was dismissed by the trial court vide order dated 08.01.2024.

The trial court while dismissing the said application has observed that PW1 was extensively cross- examined by the defence and the accused had not made any valid grounds to recall her for further cross- examination.
The said order passed by the trial court rejecting application filed by the petitioner under section 311 of Cr.P.C, on 08.01.2024 has attained finally.

Subsequently, yet another application was made by the NC: 2024:KHC:15197 petitioner under Section 311 of Cr.P.C, with a prayer to recall PW1 as well as PW9-investigating officer for the further examination.
During the pendency of the said application, a memo was filed stating that the said application would be pressed only for recalling PW9 and not for recalling PW1.
Accordingly, the said application was dismissed as not pressed insofar as it relates to prayer made to recall PW1.
Thereafter, the trial court allowed the said application and recalled PW9 for further cross- examination.
Subsequent to said order PW.9 was further cross-

examined on behalf of accused No.1.
7.
After completion of further cross- examination of PW9, the petitioner herein made yet another application under section 311 of Cr.P.C, to recall PW1.

The trial court having appreciated the fact that the petitioner had failed in his earlier two attempts and considering the fact that PW1 was extensively cross-examined and no good reason was assigned for recalling PW1 for further cross-examination, has dismissed the application filed by the petitioner under NC: 2024:KHC:15197 section 311 of Cr.P.C,
It is necessary to note that all the applications are filed by the petitioner at the stage when the case was set out for arguments on defence side.

Section 33 of the POCSO Act,
provides for procedure and power of special courts and Section 33(5) of the POCSO Act, specifically provides that special courts shall ensure that victim child is not repeatedly called before the court for testifying.
8. In the present case the victim has been extensively cross- examined on behalf of the defence.
In the application now filed by the petitioner it is stated that, PW.1 is required to be further cross-examined in view of certain contradictions found in the evidence of PW1 and PW9.
PW9 is the investigating officer and if there is any contradiction in the evidence of PW1 and PW9, the same is required to be suggested to the investigating officer and not to victim girl.
Opportunity has been already given to the defence to further cross-examine PW9.

The petitioner had not pressed his earlier application filed under section NC: 2024:KHC:15197 311 of Cr.P.C, to recall PW1 and it was pressed only against PW9 and therefore there is no justification on the part of the petitioner to file fresh application to recall PW1 after PW9 was recalled for further cross-examination by the petitioner.
Under the circumstances, trial court was fully justified in dismissing the application filed by the petitioner under section 311 of Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.
